items.title: FAA board finds 737 MAX software glitch poses no flight-safety risk
items.sum: The issue can drop VNAV mode during a reprogrammed go-around. The finding clears a hurdle for 737 MAX 10 certification, which United, American, Alaska and Ryanair are waiting on.

items.title: Air New Zealand drops service to 11 airports
items.sum: The carrier cites engine availability problems and fleet adjustments across Pacific and Americas routes.

items.title: Epic E1000 AX certified with Garmin Autoland
items.sum: The FAA approved Garmin's emergency automatic landing system on Epic Aircraft's single-engine turboprop.

items.title: Medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island leaves two dead, one missing
items.sum: A REACH Air Medical Services helicopter went down off the California coast on 1 October.

items.title: Newark Liberty plans $4.5M runway rehabilitation
items.sum: The work follows a recent incident that damaged a runway surface.

items.title: Global passenger demand slips 0.8% in August
items.sum: Middle East carriers fell 14.6%. Latin America, Africa and China domestic grew; India domestic fell 7.5%. IATA warns higher energy prices are eroding travelers' purchasing power.

items.title: Air cargo demand up 4.4% in August as load factors climb
items.sum: North America led with +6.6%. Gulf-linked lanes still contracting: Europe–Middle East -12.1%, Middle East–Asia -11.0%.

items.title: Heathrow third runway slips from 2035 to as late as 2039
items.sum: The airport called 2035 ambitious. The runway is costed at £21B within £49B of planned private investment; the Prime Minister has not endorsed it.

items.title: Vietnam's registered fleet reaches a record 258 aircraft
items.sum: Carriers are adding aircraft ahead of the Tết 2027 peak. Vietjet and Vietnam Airlines hold about 78% of the fleet.

items.title: Gulf airspace is open, but many carriers keep suspensions
items.sum: Emirates has restored 96% of its network. BA's Dubai pause runs to 25 Oct, Cathay's Dubai and Riyadh to 30 Nov, Finnair's Dubai to 27 Mar 2027. EASA still flags high risk over Gulf waters.

items.title: Boeing hands over 51 jets in August, 418 year to date
items.sum: 41 were 737 MAX. Orders were weak at 15, mostly 787s.

items.title: Airbus August deliveries up 9%, still behind its 870 target
items.sum: The A321neo led with 26 deliveries in the month. Airbus needs a sharp year-end ramp to reach its goal.

items.title: Gia Binh airport site clearance near complete, test flights by year end
items.sum: Tower, VIP terminal and runway are being built in parallel so the airport can serve APEC 2027.

items.title: Jet fuel up 121% in a year, with Japan and India hit hardest
items.sum: Currency moves amplified the shock: +173% in yen and +170% in rupees, against +86% in Brazil and Mexico. Airlines hedged about a third of 2026 consumption.

items.title: ACV proposes 1 December opening for Long Thành
items.sum: First routes would be Vietnam Airlines to Beijing, Hong Kong, Guangzhou, Manila and Hà Nội, and Vietjet domestic. Long-haul moves from March 2027, with 20–50% fee discounts for airlines.
